title: Flaky Layered Buttermilk Biscuits
summary: Cold butter is cut into a seasoned flour mixture, bound with buttermilk, folded twice like a letter for layers, cut and baked close together until tall and golden.
equipment: baking tray lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
very cold unsalted butter, cut into thin slices

steps.title: Cut in the butter
steps.text: Pulse the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate, sugar and salt, add the cold butter and pulse 8-10 times until the largest pieces are pea-sized.

steps.title: Bind
steps.text: Add the buttermilk and fold with a spatula until just combined into a shaggy dough.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Pat into a 30 x 20 cm rectangle, fold in three like a letter, turn and repeat once. Pat 2.5 cm thick.

steps.title: Cut and chill
steps.text: Stamp out rounds without twisting, set them touching on the tray and re-cut the scraps once to make 12. Chill 10 minutes.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Brush with melted butter and bake 14-17 minutes until tall and deep golden. Serve warm.

tips: Keep everything cold; warm butter melts into the flour and the layers disappear.
Baking the biscuits touching makes them rise taller.
A floured cutter pressed straight down gives clean edges that rise evenly.
storage: Store airtight at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Warm through before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
